versions.changelog:
openclaw-administrator v1.0.2

- Introduced a new "🛡️ EMERGENCY SAFETY PROTOCOL" section with detailed safety rules for managing configuration and installing skills.
- Added strict guidance against direct edits or overwrites of `openclaw.json`; mandate validated utility scripts and pre-bounce verification.
- Specified schema validation requirements for key changes and external skill audits prior to installation.
- Outlined a rotating backup policy and credential hygiene for all configuration changes.
- Enforced explicit authorization, requiring user confirmation and clear explanations for all system config changes.
- No changes to command workflow, triage, or agent system documentation.

openclaw-administrator v1.0.1

- Skill name updated from "openclaw-admin" to "openclaw-administrator".
- Description now emphasizes administration, expanded to explicitly cover AI model provider management (adding/configuring providers, allowlist, per-agent overrides, local/custom providers).
- Wording clarified for operations affecting provider keys and connection settings (in triage and safety sections).
- Audience guidance expanded to highlight new use cases: model setup, fallback/override, custom endpoint and integration scenarios.
- No structural changes to command workflows, safety rules, or system architecture.

Initial public release — OpenClaw CLI management and architecture documentation.

- Comprehensive skill that enables Openclaw to properly administor iteself to help you setup and configure features and functions - to operate, configure, and troubleshoot the OpenClaw, including gateway, agents, models, channels, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
- Added clear execution workflow, safety rules, and triage sequence for issue resolution.
- Detailed multi-agent architecture overview, agent workspace file structure, and routing bindings explained.
- Sub-agent spawning, workspace bootstrap file management, and channel connectivity guidance included.
- Five new documentation files: README.md and four deep-dive references (command-map, models/providers, multi-agent recipes, OpenAI HTTP API).
